ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, within the rectangle $ABCD$, point $E$ lies on the extension of $AB$. If $BE=AC=6$ and $\angle E=15^\circ$, then what is the length of $AB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect BD, \\
since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle, \\
therefore BD=AC, \\
also since BE=AC, \\
therefore BD=AC=BE=6, \\
therefore $\angle E=\angle BDE$, \\
therefore $\angle ABD=\angle E+\angle BDE=2\angle E=30^\circ$, \\
therefore AB=$BD\cos\angle ABD$=6×$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$=$\boxed{3\sqrt{3}}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the diagram, within the rectangle $ABCD$, point $E$ lies on the extension of $AB$. If $BE=AC=6$ and $\angle E=15^\circ$, then what is the length of $AB$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $BD$. Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle, therefore $BD=AC$. Also since $BE=AC$, therefore $BD=AC=BE=6$. Therefore $\angle E=\angle BDE$. Therefore $\angle ABD=\angle E+\angle BDE=2\angle E=30^\circ$. Therefore $AB=BD\cos\angle ABD=6\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\boxed{3\sqrt{3}}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is rectangle ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, and D is at the upper left; point E is to the right of B, located on the extension of the straight line on which AB lies; the figure draws the slanted line segment from D to E. Then reason: Add diagonal BD according to the method. Because ABCD is a rectangle, the two diagonals are equal, namely BD=AC. The problem statement gives BE=AC=6, therefore BD=BE=6. In triangle BDE, BD=BE, so it is an isosceles triangle, the base angles are equal, hence ∠BDE=∠E=15°. Since BA and BE are rays in opposite directions, ∠ABD is the exterior angle of triangle BDE at B, so ∠ABD=∠E+∠BDE=15°+15°=30°. In right triangle ABD, BD is the hypotenuse, therefore AB=BD·cos30°=6·√3/2=3√3.
